arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Browning argued the Act should encourage a society where race no longer matters.
He stated coalition districts bring races together by fostering political alliances.
Chief Justice Roberts questioned if coalition districts prove the Act succeeded.
Justice Alito asked for a statistical line for significant crossover voting.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act. It asks whether a district with a minority group under 50 percent can satisfy the statute. The core dispute involves the definition of a protected voting group.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the sides that brought the case want the Court to accept coalition districts as valid under Section 2.
the opposing sides want the Court to require a majority-minority composition for Section 2 claims.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the sides that brought the case argue coalition districts foster cross-racial political alliances and reduce the role of race.
the opposing sides argue that only majority-minority districts reliably protect minority voting power under the statute.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Chief Justice Roberts asked if coalition districts show the Act succeeded rather than needing broader application.
Justice Alito asked how much crossover voting statistically makes a difference in district outcomes.

paragraphs: The outcome defines how states draw legislative districts. It determines whether race remains a central factor in districting. It shapes the balance between political coalition building and minority representation.
